transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Nice to meet you. 

Well... I suppose I'm here because, for the past year or so, I just... I'm always puttering around. Fixing things, arranging... volunteering for one more thing. Even at 87, I just have a hard time sitting down and being still. That's mostly it.
Have you noticed any recent changes in your memory or your ability to keep track of daily tasks?
No... not really. My memory is fine. I keep track of what I need to do just fine.
Over the past year, have you felt consistently sad, down, or lost interest in the things you usually enjoy?
No... I wouldn't say that. I'm not sad. I still like doing my usual things.
When you are keeping yourself so busy, do you find that your mind is often filled with uncontrollable worries or fears about many different things in your life?
No... I don't really worry about things like that. I just prefer to keep moving. That's all.
When you are finally sitting or lying down, do you experience any uncomfortable sensations in your legs that make you feel like you have to move them?
No... I don't get any strange feelings like that. My legs are fine.
During these past few years, have you experienced periods where your energy is much higher than usual, where you feel like you need less sleep, or where you feel particularly talkative or impulsive?
No... I sleep the same as always. I don't have spells like that. I just go about my day.
When you try to sit still and do nothing, do you feel a sense of internal restlessness or agitation that forces you to get back up and move?

Well... I suppose. Like if I'm at the senior center meetings, or... sitting through the announcements at church. I just get this... ants-in-my-chair feeling. I end up having to shift around a lot. Or I'll stand up to get coffee, or just straighten my papers... just to get through it, I guess.
When you feel that 'ants-in-your-chair' sensation, do you also feel a sense of mental tension or psychological anxiety in those moments?
No... I don't think so. I wouldn't call it anxiety. It's really just... my body wanting to move, I suppose. I don't feel worried or anything like that in my head.
When you feel that need to move, does it feel like a physical tension that is relieved by the movement, rather than an attempt to distract yourself from a bad mood or a difficult thought?
Yes, I suppose that's right. It's just physical. Moving helps. I'm not... I'm not trying to distract myself from anything.
When you feel that need to move, would you describe the feeling as an internal sense of jitteriness or physical 'crawling' under your skin?
I... I don't know if I'd call it crawling under my skin. That sounds... a bit extreme. It's just... I just feel like I need to move. That's all.
Are you currently taking any prescription medications on a regular basis?
No, I'm not taking anything. Just... no medications right now.
Have you experienced this same 'ants-in-your-chair' feeling at any point earlier in your life, or is this something that only started within the past year?

No, it's... it didn't just start. It's been a very long time. Even back in grade school, I remember getting scolded. I'd pop out of my seat, or... talk over my classmates. They used to tell me I was just 'too lively.' That was... well, long before I was even a teenager. So, no, it's not new.
When you are working on a task, do you often find that you make careless mistakes or have difficulty keeping your attention on the details?
No... I don't really think so. I pay attention fine, I suppose. I haven't really noticed making careless mistakes.
When you have to work on something that you find boring or repetitive, do you find it difficult to keep your mind on the task until it is finished?
Not particularly, no. If a task needs doing... I just finish it. I haven't really had trouble with that.
When you have a series of tasks to complete, do you often find it difficult to organize them or keep your materials and belongings in order?
No... I don't think so. I keep my things where they belong. I haven't really had any trouble keeping things in order.
